title: Incremental PRD: Unified Gen+Sim Pairing for Hosted Endpoints (chat/completions + embeddings + rerank) — scope, acceptance, launch checklist
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Background: Customers increasingly request a single, well-documented flow to (1) generate candidate text responses (chat/completions), (2) embed those candidates for semantic comparison, and (3) rerank candidates against context-specific signals. Currently teams wire multiple API calls and ad-hoc orchestration; this PRD defines a converged surface pairing guidance, minimal server-side conveniences (batching + ephemeral embedding caching), and the launch acceptance criteria and checklist for the hosted product lane.

Goal: Ship a small-surface, developer-friendly pattern and operational support that reduces common latency and cost patterns for Gen+Sim+Rerank workloads by ~20% (unit-cost), while preserving explicit control for customers to opt out (keep independent calls). Provide stable behavioral contracts and observability for production rollout.

Non-goals: Not attempting to replace our full composite endpoint work; no changes to auth/quotas beyond existing rate limits; no new client SDKs in this phase (SDK additions tracked separately).

User stories:
- As a frontend engineer, I want a documented example flow and sample payloads to do candidate generation + similarity rerank so I can implement an instant-relevance search experience.
- As an ML infra owner, I want the platform to provide a recommended batching and ephemeral embedding-cache policy so cost and latency are predictable.
- As a customer, I want deterministic acceptance criteria that ensure quality regressions are flagged before rollout.

API surface (proposal):
- New optional request flag on standard generation endpoints: "combine_with_embeddings": { "mode": "paired_rerank", "embedding_model": "text-sim-lite-v1", "top_k": 8, "rerank_signal_weights": "[text_similarity:0.7, recency:0.3]" }  -- NOTE: this is an inline example; final wire format will be in the API spec doc linked below.
- Behavior: If flag present, server (hosted) performs: generate -> compute embedding of each candidate (server-side, can reuse prefix cache if present) -> compute similarity to supplied context embedding or compute context embedding if not provided -> produce scored list + deterministic scoring metadata.
- Fallback: Customers may set "external_embeddings": true to supply precomputed vectors and skip platform embedding compute.

Performance targets and SLOs (hosted lane):
- Median end-to-end (generate + embed candidates + rerank) for typical 3-candidate path: <= 250ms for small models on hosted tier; <= 120ms for optimized short-req path (where generation uses streaming 1-token warm path).
- 99th percentile degradation cap: no more than +150ms relative to baseline generation-only path for same traffic profile.
- Cost target: platform-side extra compute per candidate must average < 0.25 tokens-equivalent cost (quantified in runtime profiling doc).

Quality and behavioral contracts:
- Determinism: rerank outputs must be idempotent for identical inputs, with stable weight application and reproducible scoring metadata across model version pins.
- Transparent scoring: response includes per-candidate breakdown: {generation_score, sim_score, weighted_score, model_versions, embedding_model}.

Acceptance criteria (required to mark Done):
- AC1: API spec merged and published (Confluence) with wire-format examples, code snippets for REST + curl + JS sample, and opt-out pattern documented.
- AC2: End-to-end e2e test harness (unit + integration) exercised on staging with synthetic traffic and found to meet perf targets above for baseline models. (Test report attached).
- AC3: Telemetry: new dashboards created and available in Grafana: host-gen-sim-rerank-latency, per-route token-cost, per-tenant error-rate. Dashboards linked in comments.
- AC4: Canary rollout plan documented and validated with infra (runbook + throttles) and at least one canary customer signed up for early access.
- AC5: Security review completed and any KMS handling or data retention details approved by Security.
- AC6: SDK examples (sample code) in the docs repo and a minimal quickstart in the console UI (example template) added.
- AC7: Rollback criteria defined (quality/regression thresholds and latency thresholds) and automation to shift traffic if thresholds breached.

Launch checklist (operational steps and owners):
- [ ] Docs: Confluence PRD -> approved and pinned (owner: Priya). Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRD/pages/GEN-SIM-RERANK
- [ ] API: wire-format PR to api-specs repo (owner: API team) — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-specs/pull/2561
- [ ] Runtime: perf tuning merged (owner: ENG-runtime) -> PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4129
- [ ] Telemetry: dashboards + alerts created (owner: Observability) -> Grafana links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/host-gen-sim
- [ ] E2E Tests: test harness passing on staging (owner: QA) -> test report: gs://redwood-ci/reports/gen-sim/2025-11-29/report.html
- [ ] Canary: schedule canary cohort (owner: Customer Ops) and notify support playbook owners.
- [ ] Compliance: security sign-off (owner: Security) and data retention doc attached (owner: Legal).
- [ ] Runbook: update hosted-runbooks with rollback commands and a sample incident timeline (owner: SRE).
- [ ] SDK examples: quickstart + sample app in docs repo (owner: DevRel).

Rollout plan and gates:
- Stage 0: Internal-only launch (QA + engineering traffic) for 48 hours. Gate: no P0 errors and 99th percentile latency within +100ms of baseline.
- Stage 1: Canary subset (5 production customers, low traffic) for 7 days. Gate: no customer-facing quality regressions and cost telemetry within target band.
- Stage 2: 25% traffic ramp (7 days) monitored. Gate: error rates stable, no new incidents.
- Stage 3: Full ramp if all gates pass.

Monitoring/alerts and SLOs to operationalize:
- Alert A: route-error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 10 minutes -> page SRE on-call.
- Alert B: median end-to-end latency > target + 80ms -> page runtime on-call.
- Alert C: quality-regression-alert (eval harness) detects drop > 2% in top-K pass-rate on the golden prompt set -> notify PM + ML ops.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Server-side embedding compute improves end-to-end latency for most customers but adds platform costs and additional privacy surface (addresses via opt-out and KMS annotations). We prioritize opt-out and explicit data-retention flags.
- We avoided merging this with broader composite-endpoint work to reduce blast radius and unblock customers faster.

Open questions & follow-ups:
- Q1: Should we expose rerank weighting as a first-class typed param or as generic signal pluggable JSON? (Action: Product + API to decide 2025-12-05).
- Q2: How to price paired operations (bundled discount vs additive token accounting)? (Action: GTM + Finance to propose by 2025-12-10).
- Q3: Which embedding models are allowed by default in hosted due to cost/latency constraints? (Action: ML infra to publish recommended list).
